explain_en: 이를 닦다 means the same thing. In conversation, 양치(하다) is heard more often.

I didn't hear my alarm and overslept.
I turned off the alarm and went back to sleep.

examples.en: The alarm was so loud that it startled me.

examples.en: I have to get up early tomorrow, so I set the alarm for six.

explain: 알람(alarm)과 알림(notification)은 달라요. 정한 시간에 울리면 “알람”, 휴대폰에 메시지가 오면 “알림”이에요.

examples.en: After a long time, I started missing my hometown house.
At my hometown house, my mother prepared a meal for me.

examples.ko: 방학이 되면 기차를 타고 고향집으로 돌아가요.
examples.en: When vacation comes, I take the train back to my hometown house.
There was a persimmon tree in the yard of my hometown house.

explain: '고향'이 지역을 말한다면 '고향집'은 내가 자랐거나 부모님이 사시는 집을 말해요. 결혼한 사람이 부모님 집을 말할 때는 '본가'라고도 해요. '고향집에 내려가다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: I plan to go down to my hometown house during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서울 같은 도시에서 고향으로 갈 때 '내려가다'를 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 내려가다 is often used when heading from a city like Seoul to one's hometown.
phrases.en_equiv: go down to one's hometown house

phrases.en: On the weekend I went to my parents' home and saw them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼한 사람이 부모님 집을 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by married people to refer to their parents' home.

phrases.en: I'm far away, so I miss my hometown house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떨어져 있어서 보고 싶은 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses missing home when you're far away.

explain_en: While '고향' refers to a region, '고향집' refers to the house where you grew up or where your parents live. A married person may also call their parents' house '본가'. You say '고향집에 내려가다' (to go down to the hometown house).
